# Website Proposal for Bella Notte

**Prepared by [Your Studio Name] | [Date]**

## Introduction

Bella Notte has been a Columbus favorite for years, and your website should feel as welcoming as your dining room. We'll design and build a fast, mobile-friendly site where guests can see your menu, book a table in under a minute, and find everything they need to visit. Your team will also be able to update the menu without calling a developer. We'll launch by **March 15, 2027**.

## Project Phases

**Phase 1: Discovery and Design (Weeks 1-5)**
We'll learn what makes Bella Notte special: your story, your regulars, and the experience you want guests to expect. Then we'll create the sitemap and a custom design for the homepage and key pages. You'll review two rounds of revisions before we start building.

**Phase 2: Build and Integrations (Weeks 6-12)**
We'll develop the full site (Home, Menu, Reservations, About, Gallery, Contact/Hours). We'll connect online reservations through a booking platform and set up an easy menu editor. You'll be able to change dishes, prices, and specials yourselves, and we'll test everything on phones, tablets, and desktops.

**Phase 3: Launch and Training (Weeks 13-16)**
We'll run final testing, set up local search (Google Business Profile, basic SEO), and take the site live. We'll give you a recorded walkthrough and a live training session. We'll also provide 30 days of free support after launch. This schedule leaves about a month of buffer before March 15.

## Investment

| Item | Cost |
|---|---|
| Discovery and strategy | $900 |
| Custom design (up to 6 pages, 2 revision rounds) | $1,500 |
| Site development (responsive, SEO-ready) | $1,600 |
| Online reservation integration | $600 |
| Self-service menu editor | $700 |
| Launch, training, and 30-day support | $700 |
| **Total** | **$6,000** |

**Payment:** 40% to begin ($2,400), 30% at design approval ($1,800), and 30% at launch ($1,800).

**Not included:** Domain, hosting, and reservation platform subscription fees (if any). We'll recommend options and help you set them up. Photography and copywriting are available as add-ons.

## What We Need From You

1. **Logo and brand files**, including colors and fonts if you have them
2. **Current menu**, including dishes, descriptions, and prices, plus any seasonal or special menus
3. **Photos** of the food, dining room, and team (we can recommend a photographer)
4. **Business details:** hours, address, phone, parking info, and your private dining or catering offerings
5. **Reservation rules:** table sizes, seating times, party-size limits, and any blackout dates
6. **Your story:** a few paragraphs about the family and history, or a short interview with us
7. **Account access:** your domain registrar, current website host, and Google Business Profile
8. **One point of contact** who can give feedback within 3 business days

*To keep the March 15 launch, we'd like to kick off by early December 2026. Reply to this proposal or call [phone] to get started.*

---

Two assumptions to check before you send this:
- I read March 15 as 2027, since today is October 2026. If that's wrong, the timeline needs adjusting.
- I assumed reservations run through a third-party platform like OpenTable, Tock, or Resy. A fully custom booking system would cost much more than $6,000.

I can also turn this into a formatted Word or PDF file, or adjust the tone to fit your studio's voice.

# Website Proposal: Bella Notte

**Prepared for:** The Bella Notte family, Columbus, OH
**Prepared by:** [Studio Name] | [Date] | Valid for 30 days

## Why this, why now
Bella Notte has built its reputation on a warm table and a loyal neighborhood following. The website should do the same job: make a first-time visitor hungry, then make booking a table take less than 30 seconds on a phone. We'll build a site that shows off the room and the food, takes reservations directly, and lets your team change the menu in minutes without calling a developer. It will be live by **March 15, 2027**, with two weeks of buffer built in.

## Three phases

**Phase 1: Discovery and Design (Nov 9 – Dec 18)**
- A 60-minute kickoff and a review of your current site, competitors, and Google/Yelp presence.
- Sitemap and a mobile-first design for Home, Menu, Reservations, Our Story, Private Events, and Contact/Hours.
- Two rounds of revisions. We finalize the design by Dec 18.

**Phase 2: Build and Menu System (Jan 4 – Feb 12)**
- We build the site and connect online reservations (your existing tool or one we help you choose).
- An easy menu editor: update dishes, prices, and tags (vegetarian, gluten-free), and mark items "sold out," with no code. Seasonal and special menus can be scheduled in advance.
- Local SEO basics: Google Business Profile, structured data, fast load times, and accessibility checks.

**Phase 3: Launch and Handoff (Feb 15 – Mar 15)**
- Testing on phones and desktops, plus a staff test of real reservations.
- A soft launch around Mar 1, then a full launch no later than **Mar 15**.
- A 60-minute training session for your team, a short video guide to the menu editor, and 30 days of free post-launch fixes.

## Investment

| Item | Phase | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Discovery, strategy, sitemap | 1 | $700 |
| Custom design (mobile + desktop, 2 revision rounds) | 1 | $1,600 |
| Site build, 6 core pages | 2 | $1,500 |
| Reservation integration | 2 | $600 |
| Self-service menu editor | 2 | $900 |
| Local SEO and Google Business setup | 2 | $300 |
| Testing, launch, training, 30-day support | 3 | $400 |
| **Total** | | **$6,000** |

**Payment:** 40% ($2,400) to start, 30% ($1,800) at design approval, 30% ($1,800) at launch.

**Not included (paid directly by you):** domain and hosting (about $20–35/month), and any reservation platform fees. Most platforms charge a monthly or per-cover fee, and we'll go through the options with you. Professional photography and copywriting are available as add-ons if you'd like them.

## What we need from you

1. **By Nov 13:** a signed proposal, the 40% deposit, and one decision-maker who approves designs. A single point of contact keeps us on schedule.
2. **By Nov 20:** your logo files, brand colors and fonts if you have them, and your domain registrar login (or we can help you find it).
3. **By Dec 4:** your current menus with prices, hours, address, phone, and your reservation account details if you already have one.
4. **By Dec 11:** 15–25 high-quality photos of the food, dining room, and team. We can recommend a photographer if needed.
5. **By Jan 15:** your story in your own words (a few paragraphs, rough is fine), private event details, and any press or awards you'd like featured.
6. **Within 2 business days** of each review request, your consolidated feedback. Delays here are the most common reason launches slip.

**Ready to start?** Reply to approve, and we'll send the agreement and first invoice.

[Your Name] | [email] | [phone]

---

**Things to check before you send it:**
- I assumed March 15, 2027, since today is Oct 26, 2026. All dates are placeholders to adjust to your calendar.
- The price breakdown is my suggestion. Shift the line items to match your real effort, as long as they still add up to $6,000.
- Decide which reservation system you'll recommend (OpenTable, Resy, Tock, or a lower-cost option). Restaurants care about its monthly fees more than about the integration itself.
- The Jan 15 content deadline is the biggest risk. Family businesses often get stuck writing the "Our Story" page, so offer to interview them by phone and write it for them.
